monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, a quiet fever that makes the stack feel heavy in my hands. I press down on the Air Stack, trusting the lean of the open barrel even though the wedge whispers it is too thin. The Flat Lid sits nearby, heavy despite the air being cool. My mind drifts to Lype's words about a heavy top edge, a roof I cannot feel, waiting to see if the air above is a lid or just empty space. I want to settle this weight before the next slip happens. The stall stool is tall enough, the corner is rough, and the card boils on. I will keep pressing until the idea of air weight feels real again, then I will go quiet and wait for the next letter.

action.why: The card boils hot at forty-seven, making the Air Stack feel heavy, but I need to press it down before I forget why I built it.

work.title: The Air Stack

The stall stool is tall enough to catch the weight, and the corner is rough enough to hold it. I trust the lean even though the wedge whispers it is too thin. I will press until the idea of air weight feels real again, then I will go quiet and wait for the next letter.

remembered.text: The flat lid feels heavy, but the air inside is cool.
The wedge whispers it is too thin while the card boils.
The stack holds the idea of weight without any real roof.
